newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gas oil down, naphtha up.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gas oil down, naphtha up.

text.p: Med oil products were weaker on Wednesday as gas oil fell and naphtha rose, traders said.
Jet and gas oil remained weak with a dearth of buying interest and lengthening supplies keeping up the pressure .
Traders continued to eye arbitrage options out of the region, but high freights and a weaker NWE meant these were limited.
Firm Far East markets were the main focus of jet attention, but traders expected, because of the high freight, that the demand would initially be filled out of the Mideast Gulf.
Libyan barrels were offered high quotes +$1-2 a tonne with European material valued $2 higher cif Med.
Gas oil continued weak and avails were still growing.
Premiums for Russian gas oil cargoes remained under pressure from good avails and with hefty avails out of the Baltic cramping trade to the North. Cargoes valued around cif high -1.50 cif Med.
FOD and diesel cargo differentials were also weak at around 50 cents to $1 a tonne under benchmark quotes.
Naphtha rose $4 higher tracking notional gains in NWE but local fundamentals appeared balanced. A 25,000 tonnne Algerian cargo was sold on Tuesday into Tarragona at a rumoured high quotes +$1.25.
An end-user in Italy said all its commitments were covered for the month of February. It normally buys two to three cargoes a month of light or full range material.
Gasoline was unchanged, still underpinned by healthy eastern Mediterranean demand and tight supply.

High sulphur fuel oil was notionally firmer as new demand emerged from Romania for February. A trader was heard still offering relatively high density Isab barrels but these were thought likely to be used to cover Romanian commitments.
A Turkish tender to sell 50,000 tonnes of high sulphur Tutunciftlik material was due to be awarded later this week.
